epics.title: Capability Inventory and Attachment Console
epics.objective: Expose installed capability sources in the Web UI while preserving the existing separation between inventory, agent attachment, and action authority.

tasks.title: Browser Skills facade and atomic attachment replacement
tasks.objective: Add sanitized browser-session Skills routes and a transaction-backed complete-set attachment replacement path so the console can inspect inventory, install ZIPs, read safe files, and update agent skill bindings without changing public API or CLI semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Browser-session Skills inventory, file metadata/content, install, and attachment routes enforce session auth, role scopes, Origin, CSRF, recent-reauth where required, and app isolation.
Browser DTOs and errors omit storage references, hashes, credentials, secrets, tokens, stack traces, and raw upstream errors.
ZIP installation validates packages, updates same-name skills in inventory, and does not attach agents.
Attachment saving atomically replaces the full desired set for up to 100 distinct app-scoped agents, including disabled agents, and invokes settings projection once after commit.
Declared actions remain inventory metadata only and are not granted by attachment.

required_tests.id: redacts skill inventory and rejects viewer mutations

plan_contracts.statement: Browser-session Skills inventory, file metadata/content, install, and attachment routes enforce session auth, role scopes, Origin, CSRF, recent-reauth where required, and app isolation.
Browser DTOs and errors omit storage references, hashes, credentials, secrets, tokens, stack traces, and raw upstream errors.
ZIP installation validates packages, updates same-name skills in inventory, and does not attach agents.
Attachment saving atomically replaces the full desired set for up to 100 distinct app-scoped agents, including disabled agents, and invokes settings projection once after commit.
Declared actions remain inventory metadata only and are not granted by attachment.

reviewer_focus: Load-bearing constitution references: constitution/09-agent-conduct.md, constitution/pnp-coding-standards-modular-monolith.md, constitution/pnp-api-standards.md, constitution/pnp-database-standards.md, constitution/05-logging-and-observability.md, and constitution/07-exception-handling.md.

Task-specific seam: browser route DTO mapping must remain separate from storage-bearing skill records, and attachment replacement must be one repository/service transaction rather than per-agent route loops.
Authority boundary: install and attach mutate inventory/source bindings only; declared skill actions must not become selected capabilities or hidden credential projections.

review_budget.reason: One backend vertical slice: contracts, route facade, service/repository method, route wiring, and focused tests. No schema migration or public API rewrite.

tasks.title: Skills inspection UI
tasks.objective: Build the read experience at /ui/skills: navigation, searchable split inventory/detail layout, validated URL state, Overview/Files/Actions/Agents tabs, lazy safe file preview, read-only action cards, and viewer-safe behavior.
acceptance_criteria: /ui/skills appears under Configure with the installed-skill count and restores valid skill, q, and tab search state.
The split inventory/detail layout stacks on narrow screens and preserves loading, empty, search, and error states.
Viewers can inspect sanitized inventory, overview, files, actions, and attached agents without mutation controls.
Files are loaded lazily; UTF-8 text previews render as inert text and binary files show metadata only.
Actions are read-only and attached-agent Manage access links route to the existing Agent Access tab.

tasks.title: Administrator install and attachment workflows
tasks.objective: Add admin-only ZIP install and attachment dialogs with same-name update warning, disabled-agent labels, pending/error preservation, query invalidation, and accessibility behavior while keeping attachment separate from authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Administrators can choose one ZIP, see the approved same-name update warning, install without automatic attachment, and use success actions to view the skill or attach agents.
Administrators can replace the complete attachment set from a dialog that preserves state on failure and announces success with next-run wording.
Disabled agents remain selectable and are labeled "Disabled · available when the agent is enabled."
Mutation flows invalidate Skills and affected Agent queries without exposing controls to viewer sessions.
Dialog focus, keyboard operation, labels, live status, and narrow-layout behavior follow existing Web UI conventions.
